sections.html:
Midland certifies rentals through its own city program, posts its own tax calendar and records deeds at a flat county fee. Knowing those three items lets a seller schedule a sale without surprises.

Midland is estimated at 42,806 people for 2025, up 0.3% from 2020. Owners live in 67.1% of the 18,535 households, with a median home value of $203,900 and a median rent of $1,048. Median household income is $73,325 and the average commute is 20 minutes.

Midland is the Midland County seat, built where the Chippewa River joins the Tittabawassee, roughly 24 miles northwest of Saginaw and 19 miles west of Bay City. Dow Chemical is the anchor employer, with health care and education following. Midland Public Schools and Bullock Creek Public Schools cover K-12, so confirm the district for your address.

sections.h2: Neighborhoods, utilities and the historic district
sections.html:
The city counts more than 35 neighborhoods, grouped into eight general areas. Downtown includes the Circle business district, Country Club is known for large wooded lots, and the West Main Street Historic District was set up in 1979. Inside the historic district, a commission signs off on construction, additions, repairs, moves and demolitions, so ask it before planning visible work.

City residents get weekly garbage and yard waste pickup and monthly collection of recyclables, large items and brush. Houses in unincorporated areas without municipal water rely on private wells and septic systems, which is worth stating in a listing. Consumers Energy supplies power and gas.

sections.h2: Does the May 2020 flood matter to a Midland buyer?
sections.html:
It often does. Two upstream dams, Edenville and Sanford, failed on May 19, 2020, and about 10,000 Midland residents had to evacuate in what officials called a 500-year flood.

A house that took water, or sits close to either river, sells more smoothly with a paper trail: repair invoices, permits, insurance claims and remediation records. A repaired basement with documents is easier to price than one nobody can account for.

Everyday weather leaves marks too. January highs sit near 29 degrees and snowfall runs 31.4 inches a year, so roofs, gutters and furnaces get a real test each winter.

sections.h2: What Midland requires of a house that has been a rental
sections.html:
Midland inspects and certifies each home, duplex, rooming house, short-term rental and apartment that its owner does not occupy, and the unit may not be rented until certified. That includes houses where no rent is collected and houses occupied by relatives.

A homeowner may keep up to two boarders in a single-family house without an inspection; a third renter triggers one. Four unrelated tenants is the cap for any rental unit. Fees changed on July 1, 2025 to:

  • Rooming house: $105
  • Other rental units: $79 for the first unit and $36 for each extra unit
  • First reinspection per unit: free, with later ones billed at the certification rate
  • Late certification: $36 per unit, with the full certification fee repeated at 30 and at 60 days of delay

The Rental Program takes calls at (989) 837-3383, option 1, or email at rentalprogram@midland-mi.org. Any plan to rent the house for a few months before selling it needs the certificate first.

Midland mails summer bills on July 1 and winter bills on December 1, and December 31 is Tax Day, the date that fixes the next year's value and classification. The dates stay close to constant from year to year.

Midland tax calendar
DateWhat happens
February 14Prior year's winter taxes due without penalty
March 1Unpaid real property taxes pass to the Midland County Treasurer
2nd Monday in MarchBoard of Review hears value and classification appeals
June 1Principal residence exemption filing deadline for the summer bill
September 15Summer taxes due; deadline to file a summer deferment
November 1Principal residence exemption filing deadline for the winter bill

A buyer who lives in the house by June 1 qualifies for the summer bill's exemption, and moving in by November 1 covers the winter bill. MCL 211.27a resets taxable value after a sale, so the buyer's first bill will likely differ from yours.

sections.h2: At the Midland County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Recording costs $30 for any document, however many pages it has. The office sits at 220 W Ellsworth Street and keeps weekday hours of 8 to 5.

  • A warranty deed or land contract needs a $5 certificate proving taxes are current.
  • Transfer tax runs $4.30 per $500 of the sale amount, state and county combined.
  • Copies are $1 a page and a certified copy adds $5.
  • Qualified submitters can e-record, but court orders and death certificates carry a raised seal and go in on paper.
  • The office will not draft a deed or advise on one.

Under MCL 207.526 a deed from parent to child, or grandparent to grandchild, owes no state transfer tax.

sections.h2: Which sale route suits a Midland house?
sections.html:
Match the route to your timeline and the house's condition. A listing works for a sound house with time on the calendar, a private sale for an owner who will do the legwork, and a cash purchase for a house with tenants, flood repairs or a rental certificate still pending.

Give us the Midland address and a rundown of the repairs, and we will quote a price for the house as it stands. Set that figure next to what a listing would net after repairs and fees.

sections.h2: What to gather and what happens next
sections.html:
Before you talk to buyers, collect your deed information, the latest summer and winter tax bills, and any flood repair records. If the house was rented, find the city's rental certificate and note its date. Call the Rental Program before you accept an offer from a buyer who plans to rent. At closing, the title company records the deed for $30, adds the $5 tax certificate for a warranty deed, and collects the transfer tax. Afterward, the buyer files for the principal residence exemption by June 1 or November 1, and you should rescind yours once you move out. A cash purchase skips the lender and the appraisal, so it can close on a date you pick even when repairs or a tenant remain.

If the house sits near the Chippewa or Tittabawassee, expect lenders and buyers to ask about flood history first. Have the repair invoices, permits and insurance claim papers in one folder. A buyer who sees a clean record will often ask fewer questions, and a cash buyer will price the house as it stands whatever the paperwork shows. Either way, the more of the story you can document, the smoother the closing will go for everyone involved.

faqs.q: May I rent my Midland house out while it is for sale?
faqs.a: Only after the city inspects and certifies it. The certification fee is $79 for the first unit, and each late month adds charges.

faqs.q: By what date does a Midland buyer need to claim the principal residence exemption?
faqs.a: The buyer must own and occupy the house by June 1 for the summer bill or November 1 for the winter bill, and files the affidavit with the city.

faqs.q: Who collects Midland taxes that go unpaid?
faqs.a: The Midland County Treasurer. Real property taxes still unpaid on March 1 are turned over to the county.

faqs.q: What is the recording charge for a Midland deed?
faqs.a: $30 per document covers recording. A warranty deed adds a $5 certificate, and transfer tax is billed on the sale price.

faqs.q: Should I mention the 2020 dam failures when I sell a Midland house?
faqs.a: Yes when the property flooded or lies near the Chippewa or Tittabawassee. Keep repair and insurance records handy for questions from buyers and lenders.
